headline: Ansar Allah-Saudi thread Yemen army claims 129 Ansar Allah killed in Taiz strikes
dek: Yemen's army says air strikes on Ansar Allah targets in Taiz governorate (13 strikes on positions/weapons/vehicles incl. 60th Street, Taiz Airport, Al Rabiei, Dhubab, Al Maafir, Al Masrakh) killed 129 fighters and wounded 176 over 48 hours.
sources: Yemen government army statement (via Al Jazeera liveblog)
fault_line: Is the Saudi air campaign deterring anything — or feeding the escalation it claims to stop?

sections.what_happened: Yemen's army says air strikes on Ansar Allah targets in Taiz governorate (13 strikes on positions/weapons/vehicles incl. 60th Street, Taiz Airport, Al Rabiei, Dhubab, Al Maafir, Al Masrakh) killed 129 fighters and wounded 176 over 48 hours. Ansar Allah-run Health Ministry: Sunday airstrike on Sahar district, Saada killed at least 9 (incl. 5 children, 2 women), wounded 19; blames Saudi Arabia; no Saudi comment.
sections.what_verified: Al Jazeera liveblog carried both claims. 129-killed figure is government-side only; casualty split Saada from Ansar Allah ministry via AP Sunday digest (covered in prior scans).
sections.what_disputed: No independent verification of Taiz toll; Ansar Allah claims of Saudi-strike casualties single-sourced to Ansar Allah health ministry; Saudi silent on both.
sections.why_matters: The Yemen war keeps counting bodies on both sides' ledgers. Both ledgers are theirs; the dead are not.
sections.context: Background: Ansar Allah-Saudi thread update: Yemen army claims 129 Ansar Allah killed in Taiz strikes; Saada toll detail

totw_analysis: Our read: The Yemen war keeps counting bodies on both sides' ledgers. Both ledgers are theirs; the dead are not. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Saudi air campaign deterring anything — or feeding the escalation it claims to stop?
